data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim defines a binary iff: resumption is permitted when trailing bytes are identifiable as an incomplete uncommitted fragment (non-event), and refused when trailing bytes are indistinguishable from a corrupted complete event. But SRC_001's own countercondition identifies a third case — budget exhaustion between a data write and a mandatory commit record, leaving a structurally complete yet logically uncommitted event. Such bytes are neither an 'incomplete, uncommitted fragment' (they are structurally complete) nor 'indistinguishable from a corrupted complete event' (the checksum may be valid). The claim's iff leaves this intermediate case unadjudicated, failing the problem's demand to determine 'exactly when' resumption may proceed.
